Model card: MarioStudent (Core ML) A 9.0M-parameter pixel policy that plays Super Mario Bros. (NES) on the Apple Neural Engine. It is a MobileNetV3-Large that looks at the screen around Mario (now and 4 frames earlier) and picks one of 11 eight-frame moves: run, walk, hold, jump, hop, up, left, leftjump, wait, swim, down. It was trained by imitation on a save-state beam-search solver that clears all 32 levels, plus DAgger rounds, with auxiliary tile and enemy grid targets. It was not distilled from JEV. - : fp16, 17 MB, all 185 ops on the Neural Engine, about 0.5 ms per decision (M5 Pro). Its move choice matches PyTorch on CPU, GPU and ANE. - : the PyTorch checkpoint. - : inputs, outputs and move order. Results 32 levels × 3 start offsets: | | Flags | Levels cleared at least once | Cleared every time | |---|---|---|---| | Model alone | 53/96 | 23 | 12 | | Model + lookahead | 78/96 | 30 | 21 | Lookahead: before each move, candidate moves are simulated on an emulator save state, each followed by the model's next 6 moves, and the first that survives and gains ground is played. With lookahead the result is the model plus emulator simulation, not the network alone. The maze castles 4-4 and 8-4 are not cleared. Input / output - Input : [1, 6, 120, 96] fp16 in [0, 1]. RGB now, then RGB 4 frames earlier, covering 32 px behind Mario to 160 px ahead, every 2nd pixel of the 256×240 NES frame. - Output : 11 move logits (order in ), then 11 survival logits. - Moves are 8-frame button macros.
